Shri Sudhanshu Vyas Pl appearing on behalf of Advocate General  _____________________________________________________
_ __  Record of the trial Court has been received.
Heard on admission.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A. no. 1799/2022, which is an application filed und section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay.

As per the Registry report, this appeal has been filed within   therefore, the I.A stands disposed of.
 Also heard on I.A nos.10974/2022 and 6756/2022 which are the  applications filed under section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C on behalf of appellant  Ajay @ Raja for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

The appellant has been convicted under section 376(2)(n) and 5  II of IPC and sentenced to undergo ten years R.I with fine of Rs. 8000/-
 and seven years R.I with fine of Rs. 2000/- respectively with default  stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant  an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is  in jail since 14/04/2017.
The prosecutrix (PW-1) is a major lady.
Her  testimony does not inspire confidence.
She has deposed in different  version before the trial Court and during trial.
Statement of Navrang  (PW-2) is also doubtful.

sentences.text: Learned GA for the respondent/State opposed the prayer for gra of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant by submitting that prosecutrix (PW-1) has supported her version of FIR and mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) also suipported the prosecution story, which is well supported by statement of Dr. Rupali Joshi (PW-4).
As per the MLC report (Ex.-P/2), hymen of the prosecurix was found ruptured and she was feeling pain on her vagina and anus also.
The appellant could not even prove his defence.
The appellant has committed heinous offence by outraging the modesty of a girl.
Under these circumstances, the appellant does not deserve for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties as also taking note of the fact that present appellant is an auto-rickshaw driver; he misused his position and as per the statement of prosecutrix (PW-1) and her mother (PW-2), the prosecutrix was keeping on faith on the appellant, but he took her in a deserted forest at night and on the pin point of knife,
he committed rape upon her several times; statement of Dr. Rupali Joshi (PW-4) and MLC report Ex.-P/2 also corroborate the prosecution story and as per the MLC report, prosecutrix's hymen was found ruptured and she was feeling pain on her private part, hymen and anus; in view of the material evidence available on record against the appellant, this Court is not inclined to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, both the applications i.e. I.A nos.10974/2022 and 6756/2022 stand dismissed.
List the matter in due course.
CC as per rules

. 
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE amol Ajay @ Raja @ Pepsi @ Yogesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29217441/
